clue.text: Whale hump nursed by princess

indicators.note: being nursed by someone means being held in their arms, so the princess's name wraps round the other piece

parts.note: Bea is the familiar name of Princess Beatrice
to hump something is to carry it heavily, to lug it

explanation.surface: A princess cradling a heavy load, or perhaps a camel's hump, in her arms.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Beatrice, a granddaughter of Queen Elizabeth II, is known as Bea.
explanation.definitionFit: A white Arctic species of toothed cetacean, so a specific example of the general term.

clue.text: One shy of seven?

parts.note: of the seven dwarfs in Snow White, the timid one; shy of seven also suggests six

explanation.walkthrough: 'One shy of seven' reads as six, but it means the shy member of the seven dwarfs.
explanation.definitionFit: The dwarf named for his timidity in Disney's Snow White.

clue.text: Rounded parts of spheres, no apex

indicators.note: in a down clue the apex is the top letter, which is removed

parts.note: globes are spheres

explanation.surface: Curved sections of balls, with no peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Ears, lungs and brains have rounded projecting sections given this anatomical name.

clue.text: Warming device one's tucking into slit?

parts.note: a gash is a long cut or slit
someone tucking into food is an eater

explanation.surface: A heater that something is being slipped into, through a slot.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, one who is tucking into a slit is a 'slit eater', put in the right order.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic appliance burning fuel from the mains to warm a room.

clue.text: All to play for, with raise to pocket

parts.note: to jack something up is to raise it
to pot is to pocket a ball, as in snooker

explanation.surface: A poker player raising the stakes and hoping to pocket the whole pile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' and 'pocket' sound like poker and pool terms in the surface, but each is just a synonym here.
explanation.definitionFit: The biggest prize, everything at stake in a game or lottery, is the whole pool to be won.

clue.text: A bloomer, one abandoning ally and old writer, virtually

indicators.note: one abandoning means the letter for one leaves the word

parts.note: to ally is to join
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: virtually means almost, so the last letter is missing

parts.note: a quill was the old pen for writing

explanation.surface: A mistake by someone deserting a friend and an elderly author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant yellow narcissus is a spring flower, something that blooms.

clue.text: Kindness ultimately lacking in vast wit

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: cosmic means vast, on the scale of the universe

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A humourist with an enormous sense of humour but no kindness at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A wit is a person who amuses with clever jokes, like a comedian.

clue.text: Salesman's turned up, very difficult to continue

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means written upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
severe means very hard or difficult

explanation.surface: A salesman has arrived, finding it very hard to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Salesman's stands for 'has', a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going in spite of difficulty is to persist, carrying on.

clue.text: Time frames for courses

parts.note: racks are frames for holding things

explanation.surface: Temporal structures used for routes of study.
explanation.definitionFit: Courses and paths are routes followed, like running circuits.

clue.text: Copy Greek character has to tear up

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: up here means stirred or broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek has to rip up a copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear up' reads as a phrase meaning rip apart, but 'up' alone shuffles 'tear'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pirate is to copy illegally, making bootleg versions.

clue.text: A Winter's Tale character is absent — a mistake?

indicators.note: a mistake suggests the letters have been put down wrongly, so they are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a character missing from the play is an error.
explanation.walkthrough: Every themed clue says 'A Winter's Tale character' but means Twelfth Night, a winter festival tale, not Shakespeare's The Winter's Tale.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the shipwrecked twins in Twelfth Night, the play named for a midwinter feast.

clue.text: A Winter's Tale character with perfect stuff about

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the combined letters are read from the end

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with 1 standing for the letter I
to stuff something is to ram it in

explanation.surface: A character and some ideal material, with the word about tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 gives AI, the digit 1 read as the letter I. The theme is Twelfth Night, a winter festival tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivia's witty gentlewoman in Twelfth Night, who forges the letter that fools Malvolio.

clue.text: A Winter's Tale character's endless rot

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to fester is to rot or putrefy

explanation.surface: A character's ceaseless decay, or a character talking endless rot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rot' looks like nonsense talk, but it is the verb meaning to decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivia's clown and singer in Twelfth Night, the play set around a midwinter feast.

clue.text: A Winter's Tale character showing nerve after illness

indicators.note: after places the nerve word following the illness word

parts.note: ague is a feverish illness with shivering
cheek is nerve or impudence

explanation.surface: A character recovering from sickness who suddenly shows some boldness.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme is Twelfth Night, not The Winter's Tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Andrew, the foolish suitor in Twelfth Night, whose surname this is.

clue.text: Woman acting as boy, character shortly bagging a duke

indicators.note: bagging means capturing, so the shortened word holds the other letters inside
shortly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a letter is a character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An actress playing a boy, a brief character who has landed a duke, as in Twelfth Night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' is a theatrical word here but means a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A young woman who behaves like one of the lads, drinking and carousing in a boisterous way.

clue.text: Beauty cheers up after more bad breaks

indicators.note: after places the reversed word following the anagram
breaks means the letters are broken apart and rearranged
in a down clue, up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, cheers

explanation.surface: A lovely person cheers up after worse luck breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers up' looks like brightening, but is TA written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A strikingly attractive person, the ideal of the heart, is a beauty.

clue.text: Mitigate rebuke, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, so its pronunciation gives a different spelling

parts.note: teaching someone a lesson is a rebuke

explanation.surface: Asking whether softening a telling-off is the right thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: To mitigate is to reduce or make less severe, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Roughly two steps around base of device, best point of contact

indicators.note: around means the anagram goes round the other letter
roughly means carelessly arranged, so the letters are shuffled
in a down clue the base is the bottom, the last letter

explanation.surface: A dancer roughly does a two-step round a gadget, looking for the ideal contact.
explanation.definitionFit: The area of a bat or racket that hits the ball best, also the optimum point generally.

clue.text: Crank has to perform with water regulator

parts.note: a weir is a low dam controlling the flow of a river
to do is to perform

explanation.surface: An eccentric is obliged to operate a sluice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crank' could suggest a handle on a sluice, but it means an odd person.
explanation.definitionFit: A crank is an eccentric oddball, the same as a strange person.

clue.text: Old Shakespearean wino denied victory — this to add flavour?

parts.note: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters

indicators.note: denied means deprived, so the victory word is taken out

parts.note: a win is a victory

explanation.surface: An ageing Shakespearean drunk who lost; perhaps this would liven him up.
explanation.walkthrough: Regan is King Lear's second daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A herb sprinkled on food to add taste, so the clue asks if this flavours things.

clue.text: Gorge in middle of Yeovil, a tree ruined

indicators.note: the central pair of letters of the Somerset town name is taken
ruined means wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A ravine in the middle of a Somerset town, where a tree has been wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: Yeovil is a town in Somerset, England. 'Gorge' looks like a ravine but is the verb to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to stuff yourself with food, eating far too much.

clue.text: A Winter's Tale character caught up in passion is romantic

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read upwards, so the caught letters are reversed
in signals letters sitting within the following words

explanation.surface: A character swept up in passion is a romantic.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme is Twelfth Night, whose first line is spoken by this lovesick duke.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of Illyria in Twelfth Night, who opens the play with 'If music be the food of love'.

clue.text: Act of betrayal in the end, lost cause

indicators.note: the end means the final letter of the next word

parts.note: a reason is a cause

explanation.surface: A betrayal that ends up as a doomed campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost cause' looks like one phrase; split, 'lost' gives its end and 'cause' a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country or sovereign is the crime of disloyalty.

clue.text: A Winter's Tale character in the midst of hoax, raging briefly

indicators.note: in means the shortened word sits inside the middle letters
the midst is the centre, so the two central letters are taken
briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: livid means raging, furious

explanation.surface: A character caught up in a hoax, furious for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme is Twelfth Night; this countess is the target of a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The countess wooed by Orsino in Twelfth Night, who falls for the disguised Viola.

clue.text: nfinit?

parts.note: a word for boundless with its first and last letters gone, so it has lost its limits

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is the word infinite with its outer letters removed: without limits in both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Infinite things have no bounds, and the clue word has lost its boundary letters too.

clue.text: 26 or 9 inspiring a writer

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so the word takes the letter inside

parts.note: the two cross-referenced characters are the twin brother and sister of Twelfth Night

explanation.surface: Two characters inspire an author.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue numbers point to the twins of Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: The pen name of Samuel Clemens, the American author of Tom Sawyer.

clue.text: Food reliable, though not starter

indicators.note: without its starter means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: stable means steady and reliable

explanation.surface: Dependable food that comes without a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a first course, fitting the food surface, but it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A good table is a household's food and fare, as in keeping a generous table.

clue.text: A Winter's Tale character to discharge

definitions.meaning: Sir Toby, Olivia's drunken uncle in Twelfth Night, has this surname
to emit wind noisily from the stomach through the mouth

explanation.surface: A character being sent away.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Toby's surname is apt for a toper, and the word means expelling gas from the mouth.

clue.text: A Winter's Tale character one's played

definitions.meaning: the heroine of Twelfth Night, who disguises herself as Cesario
a stringed instrument that a musician plays, larger than a violin

explanation.surface: A character who has been played by an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: The disguised heroine of Twelfth Night shares her name with an alto stringed instrument.

clue.text: Breaking record, work returned is for state capital

indicators.note: breaking into means splitting a word open and inserting something

parts.note: an annal is a yearly record

indicators.note: returned means turned back, so the work word is reversed

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Smashing a record, with a work sent back, for a state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking record' looks like a sporting feat, but the record is split open.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of the US state of Maryland, home of the Naval Academy.

clue.text: A Winter's Tale character I love after soon rescuing protagonist at the end

indicators.note: after places the soon word ahead of the I and love pieces
rescuing means taking someone in, so the soon word holds the final letter

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A character loves the hero who will soon be rescued at the climax.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme is Twelfth Night, in which this sea captain rescues Sebastian.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea captain devoted to Sebastian in Twelfth Night bears this name.

clue.text: A little stout, a handsome statesman?

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Describing a man as somewhat portly but good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statesman' suggests a politician, but here it is a man from a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of a particular US state is a man of that state, read playfully.
